research.title: Peer-Reviewed Research
research.subtitle: Published academic work bridging Ethiopian food science, nutrition, and public health — from graduate research to peer-reviewed journals.
research.note: Additional publications, reports, and working papers available upon request.

papers.title: Effect of Processing and Blending on Taro and Wheat Flour Cookies
papers.authors: Abinet Tekle Hagos, Solomon Worku (Dr.Eng.), Negussie Retta (Prof.)
papers.body: A graduate thesis investigating how processing techniques and ingredient blending ratios affect the nutritional quality, texture, and sensory properties of cookies made from taro and wheat flour — advancing food science research for Ethiopian ingredients.

papers.title: Nutritional Profile of Moringa stenopetala Species Samples Collected from Different Places in Ethiopia
papers.venue: European Journal of Nutrition & Food Safety
papers.body: This study profiles the nutritional composition of Moringa stenopetala samples from multiple Ethiopian regions, examining variation in protein, micronutrients, and anti-nutritional factors — contributing critical evidence for leveraging indigenous superfoods in Ethiopian nutrition programs.

papers.title: Sensory Acceptability Trial for a Chickpea-based Ready-to-use Supplementary Food
papers.body: A sensory evaluation study testing the acceptability of a chickpea-based ready-to-use supplementary food (RUSF) among target populations — assessing taste, texture, and palatability to support scale-up of locally-produced therapeutic nutrition products in Ethiopia.

faqs.question: How do I start?
faqs.answer: Book a consultation through the Book page. We will confirm timing and what to prepare.

faqs.question: Is this medical treatment?
faqs.answer: No. NEED provides nutrition counseling and education. Medical diagnosis and treatment remain with your clinician.

faqs.question: Can sessions be remote?
faqs.answer: Availability for in-person and remote options can be confirmed when you book. [CONFIRM FORMAT WITH NEED]

faqs.question: Do you guarantee a specific weight result?
faqs.answer: No. NEED does not promise specific weight outcomes. Progress depends on many factors and is reviewed individually.

faqs.question: Will I get a meal plan?
faqs.answer: Many clients receive personalized meal guidance. Exact deliverables are confirmed during consultation.

faqs.question: How long does support take?
faqs.answer: Timelines vary. Some clients work over months; others need shorter focused support. We set expectations together.

diabetes-nutrition.summary: Nutrition education and meal strategies to support diabetes care alongside your clinical team.
diabetes-nutrition.description: Practical diabetes-focused nutrition counseling — helping you understand food choices, meal timing, and sustainable patterns that support your care plan. NEED does not replace your doctor or diabetes educator.
audience: Adults living with diabetes or prediabetes (with clinician oversight)

diabetes-nutrition.approachIntro: We align nutrition education with your clinical care and lived food culture.
approach: Review of goals and clinician guidance you already have
Education on carbohydrate patterns and balanced plates

Follow-up to refine strategies and answer questions
benefits: Clearer day-to-day food decisions
Meal ideas that fit your culture and routine
Support coordinating with your medical care plan
Education without fear-based messaging

faqs.question: Can nutrition counseling replace my medication?
faqs.answer: No. Never change medications without your clinician. NEED supports nutrition education only.

faqs.question: Do I need lab results?
faqs.answer: Sharing relevant clinician guidance or labs (if you choose) can help tailor education. It is optional unless your clinician requires it.

faqs.question: Is this suitable for type 1 and type 2?
faqs.answer: We can discuss nutrition education for different contexts, always in coordination with your medical team.

common.disclaimer: This article is for general education. It is not medical advice and does not replace care from your clinician or a personalized consultation with NEED.

ethiopian-plate-basics.title: Ethiopian plate basics for everyday health
ethiopian-plate-basics.excerpt: A simple way to build balanced plates using injera, legumes, vegetables, and familiar Ethiopian flavors.
ethiopian-plate-basics.seoTitle: Ethiopian plate basics for everyday health
ethiopian-plate-basics.seoDescription: A simple way to build balanced plates using injera, legumes, vegetables, and familiar Ethiopian flavors.
ethiopian-plate-basics.coverAlt: Ethiopian plate basics for everyday health cover image placeholder

sections.heading: Start with what you already eat
sections.body: Healthy eating does not require abandoning Ethiopian cuisine. Injera, shiro, lentils, greens, and vegetable wot can anchor a balanced day when portions and variety are intentional.

sections.heading: Build color and protein into the plate
sections.body: Aim for vegetables or legumes alongside staples, and notice how energy and fullness change when meals include fiber-rich sides. Personal targets differ — counseling can refine this for you.

sections.heading: When to get personal guidance
sections.body: If you manage a medical condition, are pregnant, or need a structured plan, book a consultation rather than relying on general articles alone.

sustainable-weight-habits.title: Sustainable habits for weight management
sustainable-weight-habits.excerpt: Why slow, personalized changes beat extreme diets — and how to think about progress without miracle promises.
sustainable-weight-habits.seoDescription: Why slow, personalized changes beat extreme diets — and how to think about progress without miracle promises.
sustainable-weight-habits.coverAlt: Sustainable habits for weight management cover image placeholder

sections.heading: Habits over hacks
sections.body: Sustainable weight management focuses on routines you can keep: meal rhythm, sleep, movement you enjoy, and food patterns that fit your culture and schedule.

sections.heading: No guaranteed outcomes
sections.body: NEED does not promise specific kilogram results. Progress depends on many factors and should be reviewed individually with appropriate clinical care when needed.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: If you want a personalized plan, use Book a Consultation. For workplace programs, use the partnerships pathway instead.

diabetes-friendly-ethiopian-meals.title: Diabetes-friendly Ethiopian meal ideas
diabetes-friendly-ethiopian-meals.excerpt: Practical plate ideas that respect Ethiopian food culture while supporting diabetes nutrition education.
diabetes-friendly-ethiopian-meals.seoDescription: Practical plate ideas that respect Ethiopian food culture while supporting diabetes nutrition education.
diabetes-friendly-ethiopian-meals.coverAlt: Diabetes-friendly Ethiopian meal ideas cover image placeholder

sections.heading: Education, not treatment
sections.body: Nutrition counseling supports diabetes care but never replaces medication or instructions from your clinician. Do not change prescriptions based on an article.

sections.heading: Familiar foods, thoughtful patterns
sections.body: Balanced plates, consistent meal timing, and awareness of carbohydrate patterns can be discussed using foods you already know — injera, legumes, vegetables, and dairy where appropriate.

sections.heading: Get tailored support
sections.body: Book a diabetes nutrition consultation for guidance matched to your clinician’s plan and your daily routine.

sodium-aware-cooking-at-home.title: Sodium-aware cooking at home
sodium-aware-cooking-at-home.excerpt: Simple kitchen swaps and seasoning ideas to support blood-pressure-conscious cooking without bland meals.
sodium-aware-cooking-at-home.seoDescription: Simple kitchen swaps and seasoning ideas to support blood-pressure-conscious cooking without bland meals.
sodium-aware-cooking-at-home.coverAlt: Sodium-aware cooking at home cover image placeholder

sections.heading: Flavor without excess salt
sections.body: Herbs, spices, garlic, lemon, and careful use of berbere-style blends can keep meals enjoyable while you watch sodium — always within your clinician’s guidance.

sections.heading: Cooking patterns that help
sections.body: Cooking more at home, tasting before adding salt, and balancing vegetables with staples are practical starting points for many households.

sections.heading: Personalize with NEED
sections.body: Hypertension nutrition counseling can turn these ideas into a plan that fits your household and medical care.

fiber-fats-and-heart-health.title: Fiber, fats, and heart-conscious eating
fiber-fats-and-heart-health.excerpt: A calm overview of dietary patterns that support lipid health — without extreme elimination diets.
fiber-fats-and-heart-health.seoDescription: A calm overview of dietary patterns that support lipid health — without extreme elimination diets.
fiber-fats-and-heart-health.coverAlt: Fiber, fats, and heart-conscious eating cover image placeholder

sections.heading: Patterns matter more than perfection
sections.body: Fiber-rich legumes, vegetables, and balanced fat choices can support heart-conscious eating. Extreme elimination is rarely the first or best step.

sections.heading: Work with your clinician
sections.body: Lab results and medication decisions belong with your medical team. Nutrition education complements — it does not replace — clinical care.

sections.heading: Go deeper
sections.body: Explore cholesterol nutrition services or book a consultation for a personalized approach.

nutrition-in-pregnancy-basics.title: Nutrition in pregnancy — basics
nutrition-in-pregnancy-basics.excerpt: General education on nourishing pregnancy with familiar foods — always alongside antenatal clinical care.
nutrition-in-pregnancy-basics.seoDescription: General education on nourishing pregnancy with familiar foods — always alongside antenatal clinical care.
nutrition-in-pregnancy-basics.coverAlt: Nutrition in pregnancy — basics cover image placeholder

sections.heading: Clinical care comes first
sections.body: Pregnancy nutrition articles are educational only. Follow your antenatal clinician’s advice for supplements, screening, and medical decisions.

sections.heading: Steady, diverse meals
sections.body: Regular meals with vegetables, legumes, staples, and adequate fluids support many pregnancies. Individual needs vary widely.

sections.heading: Ask for tailored counseling
sections.body: NEED can provide personalized maternal nutrition counseling when appropriate — never as a substitute for obstetric care.

feeding-toddlers-with-local-foods.title: Feeding toddlers with local foods
feeding-toddlers-with-local-foods.excerpt: Ideas for introducing diverse Ethiopian family foods to young children — gently and safely.
feeding-toddlers-with-local-foods.seoDescription: Ideas for introducing diverse Ethiopian family foods to young children — gently and safely.
feeding-toddlers-with-local-foods.coverAlt: Feeding toddlers with local foods cover image placeholder

sections.heading: Family foods, age-appropriate textures
sections.body: Many Ethiopian household foods can be adapted for toddlers with safe textures and gradual introduction. Watch for choking risks and follow pediatric guidance.

sections.heading: Growth is individual
sections.body: Appetite and growth patterns differ. Use your child’s clinician for growth concerns; use NEED for general nutrition education and meal planning support where relevant.

sections.heading: Language note
sections.body: Amharic clinical guidance should be human-reviewed before publication. This English draft is a placeholder structure for CMS content.

reading-nutrition-labels-simply.title: Reading nutrition labels — simply
reading-nutrition-labels-simply.excerpt: A plain-language walkthrough of packaged-food labels so you can compare products with less confusion.
reading-nutrition-labels-simply.seoDescription: A plain-language walkthrough of packaged-food labels so you can compare products with less confusion.
reading-nutrition-labels-simply.coverAlt: Reading nutrition labels — simply cover image placeholder

sections.heading: What to glance at first
sections.body: Serving size, energy, and key nutrients help you compare similar products. Labels are tools — not moral judgments about food.

sections.heading: Context beats fear
sections.body: One packaged item rarely makes or breaks a diet. Patterns across days and weeks matter more than a single label.

sections.heading: Need a plan?
sections.body: General nutrition counseling can help you apply label literacy to your real shopping and cooking routine.

sewegna-recap-green-vegetables.title: Sewegna recap: green vegetables on the Ethiopian plate
sewegna-recap-green-vegetables.excerpt: A written recap of Sewegna themes on traditional greens — collards, cabbage, Swiss chard — and everyday cooking.
sewegna-recap-green-vegetables.seoTitle: Sewegna recap: green vegetables on the Ethiopian plate
sewegna-recap-green-vegetables.seoDescription: A written recap of Sewegna themes on traditional greens — collards, cabbage, Swiss chard — and everyday cooking.
sewegna-recap-green-vegetables.coverAlt: Sewegna recap: green vegetables on the Ethiopian plate cover image placeholder

sections.heading: From screen to kitchen
sections.body: Sewegna conversations often return to Ethiopia’s green vegetables — affordable, familiar, and central to many traditional meals.

sections.heading: Campaign echoes
sections.body: Public campaigns such as Green Gursha highlighted greens alongside culinary heritage. Recaps here summarize education themes, not medical outcomes.

sections.heading: Watch more
sections.body: Visit the Sewegna archive for video episodes, and book a consultation if you want personalized meal guidance.
